question: What is the school type of the school with the highest latitude? Indicate the name of the school as well as the latitude coordinates.
clarification: If several rows tie at the cut-off, return all of them.
gold: SELECT c0, c1, c2 FROM (SELECT T1."School Type" AS c0, T1."School Name" AS c1, T2.Latitude AS c2, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY T2.Latitude DESC) AS __r FROM frpm AS T1 INNER JOIN schools AS T2 ON T1.CDSCode = T2.CDSCode) AS __t WHERE __r <= 1
gold0: SELECT T1.`School Type`, T1.`School Name`, T2.Latitude FROM frpm AS T1 INNER JOIN schools AS T2 ON T1.CDSCode = T2.CDSCode ORDER BY T2.Latitude DESC LIMIT 1

c.request:
What is the school type of the school with the highest latitude? Indicate the name of the school as well as the latitude coordinates.
If several rows tie at the cut-off, return all of them.
c.sql: SELECT T1.`School Type`, T1.`School Name`, T2.Latitude FROM frpm AS T1 INNER JOIN schools AS T2 ON T1.CDSCode = T2.CDSCode WHERE T2.Latitude = (SELECT MAX(Latitude) FROM schools)

d.request: Which school has the highest latitude, and what are its school type, name, and latitude coordinates? If several schools tie for the highest latitude, return all of them.
d.sql: SELECT SOCType, School, Latitude FROM schools WHERE Latitude = (SELECT MAX(Latitude) FROM schools)

b.request: List the school type (SOCType, or School Type from frpm), school name, and latitude of every school whose latitude equals the maximum latitude in the schools table, returning all schools tied for the highest latitude
b.sql: SELECT s.SOCType, s.School, s.Latitude FROM schools s WHERE s.Latitude = (SELECT MAX(Latitude) FROM schools)
